hypotheses.reasoning: POST /v1/notify failures come from notification-svc, which cannot reach template-svc. notification-svc v3.31.0 rolled out at 12:00:03 (#3385) and reloaded config revision 738 at 12:00:28, changing TEMPLATE_SVC_URL to http://template-svc.internal:8081 (#3490). template-svc rendered normally after that (#3499, and #3537 ok at 12:00:39), then logged no further renders. From 12:00:56 notification-svc gets ECONNREFUSED to 10.25.98.71:8081 (#3580, #3699, #3831, #4015). template-svc logged no ERROR/WARN afterward, only GC DEBUG lines, so it is silent rather than erroring. Downstream: notification-svc 503s and then api-gateway 503s on /v1/notify (#3685, #3718, #4023). The connection-refused failures are fast, not hangs, which argues against a dependency timeout. The exact trigger is unclear: the config change preceded the failure by about 12 seconds, but template-svc was serving correctly until 12:00:39, so the link is plausible rather than proven. A template-svc crash or listener loss with no logs is the main alternative. Separate issue, not the notify cause: accounts-db ran out of disk (WAL growth; #2895, #3636, #3948, #4145), which breaks account-svc writes and causes /login 500s (#3959, #3977, #4256).

The accounts-db disk-full condition is a real resource exhaustion incident (disk at 95% then 99%, 'No space left on device'), but it affects account writes and /login, not /v1/notify. Ranked low as the notify cause because notify fails on template-svc connection refusals, not on account data writes.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately check template-svc process and listener health at 10.25.98.71:8081 and restart it if it is down. Confirm that the config revision 738 TEMPLATE_SVC_URL matches the actual template-svc endpoint, and roll back notification-svc v3.31.0 / config rev 738 if it does not. Separately, free disk on accounts-db (purge WAL/binlog, expand the volume) to stop the /login 500s, and find the source of the WAL growth.
